description: Test your knowledge of MI1.{3-9,11} | General Microbiology II: Laboratory Diagnosis, Specimens & Professionalism.

cards.text: Why is DNA detection preferred over conventional morphology for pathogen identification?
cards.answer: DNA detection identifies pathogens through unique genomic sequences without requiring viable organisms or specific antibodies, enabling rapid and precise identification impossible by morphology alone.

tip.tip: Sequence = definitive identity (independent of culture viability or immune response)

cards.text: What is the bacterial DNA replication mutation rate (~10⁻⁹ per base per generation), and what is its clinical significance?
cards.answer: The rate is slow enough to maintain sequence conservation within species but fast enough for antibiotic-resistance mutations to emerge and spread under selective pressure.

tip.tip: Slow evolution, quick resistance — balance allows survival yet enables adaptation

cards.text: How do antibiotic resistance genes spread rapidly between unrelated bacterial species in hospitals?
cards.answer: Resistance genes are carried on plasmids (extra-chromosomal circular DNA) that transfer between bacteria via conjugation, enabling horizontal gene transfer across species barriers.

tip.tip: Plasmids = mobile resistance couriers; conjugation broadcasts resistance

cards.text: Describe the three temperature-dependent steps of a PCR cycle and their temperatures.
cards.answer: Denaturation (94–95°C): DNA melts. Annealing (50–65°C): primers bind to target flanks. Extension (72°C): Taq polymerase synthesizes DNA. 30–40 cycles achieve ~10⁹-fold amplification.

cards.text: What is the key advantage of qPCR (real-time PCR) over conventional PCR, and name one clinical use.
cards.answer: qPCR quantifies pathogen load in real-time using fluorescent probes (vs. yes/no endpoint detection), enabling viral monitoring (HIV/HBV/SARS-CoV-2 load) in 2–4 hours.

tip.tip: Quantification, not just presence — tracks disease burden over time

cards.text: What is CBNAAT/GeneXpert, and why is it preferred for TB diagnosis under NTEP in India?
cards.answer: CBNAAT is an integrated real-time PCR cartridge that detects *Mycobacterium tuberculosis* AND rifampicin resistance (*rpoB* mutations) simultaneously in 2 hours — rapid, reliable, widely deployed.

tip.tip: TB + drug resistance in one 2-hour test — integrates diagnosis + susceptibility

cards.text: Compare Sanger sequencing and whole-genome sequencing (NGS) for microbial diagnostics.
cards.answer: Sanger: targeted sequencing of specific genes (e.g., *rpoB*, *katG* for TB resistance) in 24–48 h. NGS/WGS: sequences entire genome for outbreak tracing and comprehensive resistance profiling.

tip.tip: Sanger = focused gene, NGS = entire genome — precision vs. big picture

cards.text: Name three clinical applications of nucleic acid hybridization (probe-based detection).
cards.answer: DNA probes for confirmatory testing (*Mycoplasma*, *Legionella*, gonorrhea); in situ hybridization for tissue-specific detection (e.g., EBV in lymphoma); microarrays for simultaneous typing (HPV genotypes, respiratory viruses).

tip.tip: Probes find their partners — complementary binding = specific detection at multiple scales
